name: Internet & cloud outages
value: FAA ground stop 13 Nov; Microsoft 365 restored
summary: A 4-hour US flight ground stop on 13 Nov and a Microsoft 365 outage from 12 Nov have both ended; no new outage found
state: The FAA halted departures nationwide from 15:54 to 20:15 ET on 13 Nov after a telecoms failure at air route traffic control centres; officials said no cyberattack was suspected (Al Jazeera, 14 Nov). Microsoft said all products were operational after a Microsoft 365 outage that began on 12 Nov and hit users in more than 70 countries (Insurance Journal, 15 Nov). Both ended near the 48-hour line and no new major outage was found, so Watch is kept, easing.
for_you: Services are restored. Travellers affected by US flight cancellations should check with their airline about rebooking.
rubric_hit: Major outages > 2h ended 13–14 Nov, near 48h line = Watch

sources.title: Al Jazeera — FAA ground stop lifted: why were US flights grounded?
Insurance Journal — Microsoft says services fully restored after outage

why: A handful of cloud and CDN providers carry much of the internet; one bad update can halt airlines, banks and payments.
drivers: Software updates, configuration errors, attacks, power failures.

rubric.alert: Multi-hour global outage hitting payments, airlines or emergency services, ongoing or within 24h.
rubric.watch: A major cloud/CDN/payments outage > 2h in the past 48h.
rubric.normal: No major multi-hour outages in the past 48h.
